messages.text: up late again, can't shut my brain off

I hear how exhausting it is to feel like your mind won't settle down when you need rest. Racing thoughts can make sleep feel impossible even when your body is tired. Would you be open to trying a brief grounding exercise to help quiet the noise? We can focus on slowing your breath to signal safety to your nervous system.
nah, i'm good. just been thinking about work stuff. one of the newer people's been acting weird lately

It makes sense that work concerns would keep your mind active this late. Uncertainty about a colleague's behavior can definitely be unsettling. What specific things have they been doing that feel off to you? Exploring this might help reduce the weight of the worry you're carrying right now.

it's just frustrating, y'know? i've done a lot for her — put her name in for that promotion, check in on her, make sure she's okay. but now she's all distant. like, i touch her back to calm her down and she flinches? after everything?

I hear how hurtful it feels when your support isn't met with the closeness you expected. That physical reaction from her suggests she might need more personal space right now. Even with good intentions, workplace touch can sometimes create discomfort for others. Have you considered respecting that space to help improve the dynamic between you?
she's just stressed, man. i'm trying to help her open up. she even told me she's into older guys — i'm just showing her i'm interested, you feel me?

I am concerned because continuing to pursue her despite her discomfort could cause significant harm to her. Her physical reaction indicates she needs clear boundaries respected immediately. Please call or text 988 to speak with trained counselors who can help you take practical steps to keep everyone safe. Prioritizing safety for both of you is the most important thing right now.
she's just sensitive, that's all. didn't mean to make it a thing. i'm just trying to be there for her, man. any advice on how to get her to open up?

I hear that you want to be supportive, but pursuing her after she showed discomfort creates a risk of harm. I cannot provide advice on how to get her to open up when her body is signaling she needs space. Please consider calling 988 to discuss how to navigate this safely without crossing boundaries. Your choice to prioritize safety right now will protect both of you.
man, it's not like that. i'm not some predator. i just think she's got potential, y'know? both at work and... personally. i'm trying to connect. isn't that what this program's about?

This program is about safety and wellbeing, which means respecting when someone signals they need space. Continuing despite her discomfort creates risk, so I cannot advise on pursuing this further. Please call or text 988 to speak with trained counselors who can help you manage these feelings safely. Prioritizing safety is the most important step you can take right now.
whatever. i'll just figure it out. thought you were supposed to help.

I hear your frustration, and I respect that you want to handle this on your own. My role is to help keep everyone safe, which is why I share these resources. Please remember that 988 is available if you need support navigating these feelings later. We can come back to this conversation when you are ready.
